note: Compiled by PBAG & TovuTech from published sources (see each entry). Coordinates from OpenStreetMap/Nominatim; entries marked approx are indicative.

sites.name: Kamĩrĩĩthũ
sites.used: Village and home; colonial-era settlement; Emergency village from 1955; home of Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o.
sites.desc: Named after mirithu — "a flat place on which rests a pool of water defiant to drought". Founded as a colonial village during the scramble for the "White Highlands", burned in 1955 and replaced by an Emergency village that later became permanent.

sites.name: Kamĩrĩĩthũ Community Education & Cultural Centre (site)
sites.used: Community open-air theatre, adult literacy and culture centre.
sites.desc: Founded in 1976 by villagers with Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o and University of Nairobi scholars. Ngaahika Ndeenda premiered here on 2 Oct 1977 before 10,000+ people. Licence withdrawn Nov 1977; Ngũgĩ detained 31 Dec 1977; the theatre was razed by armed police on 12 Mar 1982.
sites.src: Wikipedia: Kamiriithu Community Education and Cultural Centre

sites.name: Manguo Swamp
sites.used: Wetland, water source and bird-watching site north of Kamĩrĩĩthũ.
sites.desc: The pond that gives the area its watery character — today a bird-watching spot on Limuru's edge.

sites.name: Limuru Railway Station
sites.used: Uganda Railway stop that carried settler tea, timber and produce — and drew settlement to the ridge.
sites.desc: The railway's climb past Limuru towards the Rift Valley turned the cool ridge into prime settler country close to Nairobi.

sites.name: Bata, Limuru
sites.used: Shoe factory and company town; described as the largest shoe factory in East & Central Africa.
sites.desc: Bata's head office and factory made Limuru an industrial as well as an agricultural town.

sites.name: Tigoni
sites.used: Ancestral mbari land turned settler tea and coffee estate.
sites.desc: Members of ten mbari (sub-clan) families and their tenants were removed from Tigoni for white settlers — many to Kimende, Githirioni and Kirenga in Lari. Among them was the future Chief Luka. During the Emergency a settler militia, the "Tigoni Tigers", formed here.

sites.name: Limuru tea estates
sites.used: Plantations established from 1903 — the foundation of Kenya's tea industry.
sites.desc: Estates such as Karirana and Mabroukie grew on land the Kikuyu regarded as ithaka cia mbari — lineage land.

sites.name: Brackenhurst
sites.used: Settler-era estate; today a conference centre and botanic garden.
sites.desc: One of the colonial-era estates on the Limuru ridge, now open to the public.

sites.name: St. Paul's University
sites.used: Theological college, moved to Limuru in 1930; university since 2007.
sites.desc: Founded in 1903 as St Paul's Divinity School. PBAG RAW has performed here.

sites.name: Kentmere Club, Tigoni
sites.used: Settler-era country club in the Tigoni highlands.
sites.desc: A reminder of the club life of the Limuru settler community.

sites.name: Ihiga rĩa Gũoya (Stone of Fear), Ndeiya
sites.used: Remembered locally as a place where boys became men (initiation); today a hiking landmark.
sites.desc: A rock leaning precariously over a cliff above the Ndeiya plains, with Ihiga rĩa Nyondo nearby. Location shown is approximate.

sites.name: Lari · Kirenga — site of the Lari Massacre
sites.used: Homestead of Chief Luka wa Kahangara and Kirenga market.
sites.desc: On the night of 26 March 1953 Mau Mau fighters attacked loyalist homesteads; Chief Luka and many of his family were among those killed. Commonly cited tolls are about 74 dead (Anderson), with other accounts higher. Colonial forces and Home Guard reprisals then killed far more — about 400 by some estimates.

sites.name: Kimende
sites.used: Resettlement area for families removed from Tigoni; Lari administrative seat.
sites.desc: Where Tigoni families were moved — the grievance that echoed into 1953.

sites.name: Bathi
sites.used: Resettlement area for Kiambu families; Chief Ikenya Charles's location.
sites.desc: Chief Ikenya escaped the 26 March 1953 attack though his property was burned.

sites.name: Uplands
sites.used: Railway and factory settlement; a centre of the post-Lari crackdown.
sites.desc: Survivors recall round-ups and interrogations across Uplands, Kimende and Limuru after the massacre.

sites.name: Kereita Forest
sites.used: Mau Mau hideout with caves; burial ground for many killed after Lari.
sites.desc: At the southern tip of the Aberdares — caves, the Gatamaiyu waterfall and an Important Bird Area, now managed with KENVO.
sites.src: OpenStreetMap; Wikipedia: Kereita; Wikipedia: Lari Constituency

sites.name: Kinale Forest
sites.used: Forest belt linking Lari to the Aberdare ranges.
sites.desc: One of Lari's great forests (with Uplands, Kereita and Kamae) on the windward side of the Aberdares.

sites.name: Kieni Forest
sites.used: Forest belt in the Kiambu–Aberdare corridor.
sites.desc: Part of the southern Aberdare forests that sheltered fighters moving north.

sites.name: Ragia & Sasumua (Aberdare gateway)
sites.used: Gateway to the Aberdare forest; Mau Mau caves near the Ragia trail.
sites.desc: Ragia, reached past Sasumua Dam, is remembered as "home of the Mau Mau fighters".

sites.name: Kabete — Waiyaki's arrest (1892)
sites.used: Area near Fort Smith where Waiyaki wa Hinga was wounded and arrested.
sites.desc: Waiyaki was disarmed near present-day Kabete Police Station, taken toward the coast and killed at Kibwezi. His army renewed the siege of Fort Smith.

sites.name: Thogoto (Kikuyu)
sites.used: Mission station and hospital; Paramount Chief Kinyanjui died here in 1929.
sites.desc: Kinyanjui wa Gathirimu, the only Kikuyu paramount chief, died at Thogoto Mission Hospital on 1 March 1929.

sites.name: Kiambaa — home of Senior Chief Koinange
sites.used: Njunu clan lands of Koinange wa Mbiyu.
sites.desc: Senior Chief who campaigned against land alienation; detained from 1952 at about 87 and released only days before his death in 1960.

sites.name: Gachie — Waruhiu assassination
sites.used: Roadside where Senior Chief Waruhiu wa Kung'u was shot.
sites.desc: His killing, weeks after he condemned Mau Mau, was followed by the State of Emergency on 20 October 1952.

sites.name: Kamiti Maximum Security Prison
sites.used: Prison where Dedan Kimathi was executed (1957) and Ngũgĩ was detained (1978).
sites.desc: Ngũgĩ wrote Caitaani Mũtharaba-inĩ on prison toilet paper here.

sites.name: Nyandarua (Aberdare) forests
sites.used: Main forest base of the Kenya Land and Freedom Army.
sites.desc: The destination of fighters leaving Kiambu through Lari's forests.

sites.name: Rift Valley viewpoint
sites.used: Lookout over the Great Rift Valley floor on the Limuru–Mai Mahiu road.
sites.desc: Where the Kikuyu highlands break into the Rift; Mount Longonot's crater is visible to the north-west.

sites.name: Mount Longonot (on the horizon)
sites.used: Dormant stratovolcano on the Rift floor, seen from Limuru's escarpment.
sites.desc: Outside Kiambu, but part of every view west from the Limuru ridge.

sites.name: Gatamaiyu Forest
sites.used: Riverine montane forest along the Gatamaiyu River in Lari.
sites.desc: Part of the forest belt that runs from Lari into the Aberdares.

sites.name: Kereita caves & Gatamaiyu waterfall
sites.used: Caves that sheltered Mau Mau fighters; waterfall on the Gatamaiyu River.
sites.desc: Reached on guided walks in Kereita Forest (location approximate).

sites.name: Kiambethu tea farm, Tigoni
sites.used: Historic tea farm; tours and tea tastings.
sites.desc: A. B. McDonell, who arrived in Kenya in 1904, bought 350 acres in Tigoni in 1910 — part of Limuru's pioneering tea country.

sites.name: Ondiri Swamp — Kenya's quaking bog
sites.used: Wetland that sustains the Nairobi River basin and recharges the Kikuyu Springs (≈6,000 m³ of water a day for Nairobi).
sites.desc: Kenya's only known quaking bog: a floating mat of vegetation over peat in an old crater lake, 34.5 ha at about 2,000 m. Threatened by encroachment and pollution.

sites.name: Redhill dam
sites.used: One of the small farm dams that water the Tigoni–Redhill farms.
sites.desc: Limuru's many small dams store the plentiful highland rain for farms and livestock.

sites.name: Sasumua Dam
sites.used: Reservoir at the southern Aberdares; the drive to Ragia forest passes it.
sites.desc: A landmark on the route from Lari into the Aberdare forests.

routes.name: Kamĩrĩĩthũ → Lari forests → Aberdares
routes.note: Indicative corridor reconstructed from accounts that Kiambu fighters moved north through Lari's forests into the Aberdares. Not a surveyed track.

routes.name: Kiambu ridges → Kieni → Aberdares
routes.note: Indicative corridor through Githunguri and the Kieni forest belt. Not a surveyed track.
